title: Data for Good Hackathon
text:
The challenge
A nonprofit partner wanted to know what was driving student growth across its programs and which groups of students needed different kinds of support.

title: Data for Good Hackathon
text:
What we built
Our team of five combined regression, to estimate which factors were associated with growth, with k-means clustering, to group students with similar profiles. Together they pointed to specific segments and regions where an intervention would likely do the most good.

title: Data for Good Hackathon
text:
Takeaway
Working against a hackathon clock with a real stakeholder pushed us to keep the analysis explainable: the output had to be something program staff could act on the next week.

title: Dog Breed Discovery
text:
The question
Fine-grained categories like dog breeds are expensive to label. We asked whether a model pretrained on generic images already “knows” breed structure well enough to cluster breeds correctly without seeing a single breed label.

title: Dog Breed Discovery
text:
Approach
We used ResNet-18, VGG-16, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/16 as frozen feature extractors across four datasets, clustered the embeddings, and scored the clusters against true breeds using the Adjusted Rand Index. We also tested whether extra preprocessing such as background removal helped.

title: Dog Breed Discovery
text:
Findings
Vision Transformers won clearly, and we traced why: the CNNs pool foreground and background uniformly, so a dog photographed on grass ends up close to other grass photos. Attention lets the ViT focus on the animal itself. The advantage held across both cat and dog datasets.

title: Dog Breed Discovery
text:
Recommendation
Deploy a frozen Vision Transformer as is. No extra preprocessing and no fine-tuning were needed, which makes the improvement close to free in engineering cost.

title: AskTemoc
text:
The problem
Answers to common student questions are spread across hundreds of catalog pages. AskTemoc lets students ask in plain language and get an answer grounded in the official catalog.

title: AskTemoc
text:
My part
I work on retrieval. Catalog pages are crawled with Crawl4AI, split into 2,000+ chunks, embedded, and stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector. A FastAPI service retrieves the most relevant chunks and passes them to a local model served through Ollama.

title: AskTemoc
text:
Measuring before changing
I am designing the evaluation harness: precision@k and recall@k for whether the right chunks come back, MRR for whether they come back near the top, and faithfulness for whether the answer actually sticks to them. Any change, such as hybrid keyword plus vector search, has to beat the baseline on these before it ships.

title: Anime Watch Planner
text:
The problem
Picking something to watch with friends usually means scrolling for twenty minutes and settling. Most recommenders are built for one person. I wanted a planner that understands a group, lets people search by mood instead of exact titles, and gets better as the group rates what they watch.

title: Anime Watch Planner
text:
What I built
Data pipeline. A PySpark job pulls 5,000+ titles from the AniList API, cleans and deduplicates them through Delta tables, and upserts them into a Lakebase (Postgres) store, so re-running the pipeline never creates duplicates. The schema covers users, groups, members, anime, ratings, watchlists, and recommendations.
Semantic search. A Databricks Vector Search index over synopses, tags, and genres lets someone ask for “something cozy with found family” rather than needing to know a title.
Learning group taste. A LinUCB contextual bandit scores titles for each group and updates from every rating, balancing what the group already likes against trying something new.
The agent. A LangGraph agent with 18 tools turns natural-language requests into tool calls that run parameterized SQL. One chat interface handles search, side-by-side comparison, watchlist management, and rating, with multi-turn memory. It is deployed as a Databricks App.

title: Anime Watch Planner
text:
What I learned
Keeping the agent’s tools narrow and the SQL parameterized made it far more reliable than letting the model write queries. The bandit was the most satisfying piece: it is a small amount of math that makes the product feel like it is paying attention.

title: Credit Card Balance Prediction
text:
The goal
Predict a cardholder’s balance from attributes like income, credit limit, and rating, in a way an underwriter could rely on.

title: Credit Card Balance Prediction
text:
What I did
Every modeling choice was checked against cross-validated error, not just in-sample fit, including which outliers to remove and which transformations to apply.
Credit limit and rating turned out to be nearly the same variable (VIF of 76 to 79), which makes coefficients unstable. I resolved it by removing one of them and then confirmed the model stayed stable across 18 stepwise-selected variants.

title: Credit Card Balance Prediction
text:
Why it matters
A point prediction alone is hard to act on. Reporting a ±$196 interval at 95% confidence gives a decision maker a sense of how much to trust each estimate.

title: Income Classification for Credit Risk
text:
The question
Income is a common input to credit risk estimates. Using 32,561 census records, I tested whether a more complex model is worth it when the decision may need to be explained to a regulator or an applicant.

title: Income Classification for Credit Risk
text:
Approach
I compared logistic regression, a decision tree, k-nearest neighbors, and a neural network, and handled a 76/24 class imbalance so accuracy would not hide poor performance on the minority class.

title: Income Classification for Credit Risk
text:
Recommendation
The neural network gained only 0.001 AUC. In a regulated credit context that is not worth giving up interpretability, so I recommended logistic regression, whose coefficients can be read and defended.

title: Income Classification for Credit Risk
text:
Delivery
I shipped an interactive presentation with two tracks: a business narrative for decision makers and a technical narrative for reviewers who want the modeling details.
